description.value: Hike-in backcountry campsite at a remote alpine lake in Garibaldi Park, reached via the demanding Singing Pass trail from Whistler; expect self-sufficient wilderness conditions, no vehicle access, and a multi-hour approach on foot.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies Russet Lake Campgrounds as a backcountry campsite within Garibaldi Provincial Park; the linked website is the general Garibaldi Park BC Parks page, which mentions Russet Lake only by name under the 'Singing Pass' safety section. No Russet Lake-specific amenity details appear anywhere in the website content. The park page confirms backcountry self-sufficiency requirements and prohibits motorized vehicles, dogs, and campfires, but provides no data on facilities at Russet Lake specifically.
concerns: The OSM website URL points to the general Garibaldi Park overview page, not a dedicated Russet Lake Campgrounds page — no site-specific amenity, booking, or contact information is available.
No address, phone, or email present in OSM record.

Backcountry location (Singing Pass area) means the campsite is inaccessible by bicycle; the park prohibits motorized vehicles and trail bikes on backcountry routes, and standard bicycles are not practical on hiking-only trails to Russet Lake.
All optional amenity fields are null due to absence of evidence — a campground-specific page or ranger contact would be required to verify facilities.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Russet Lake Campgrounds is a legitimate BC Parks backcountry campsite, but it is accessible only via a multi-hour hike from the nearest trailhead, placing it well outside practical reach for loaded touring cyclists. The linked website provides no Russet Lake-specific amenity data, making it impossible to confirm any WWC checklist criteria; a dedicated backcountry campground page or on-the-ground inspection would be needed before including this listing.
enrichment_extras.notes: BC Parks general contact: parkinfo@gov.bc.ca or 1-800-689-9025. A Russet Lake-specific page may exist under the BC Parks reservation system (Discover Camping) and could yield facility details not present on the park overview page.
